novel_features.name: Cash-flow forecast / maturity ladder
novel_features.description: Week-by-week projection of cash landing back, with maturities shifted to real settlement dates across all entities.
novel_features.rationale: Joins holdings' maturity dates to the holidays settlement calendar and buckets by adjusted date; no single API call applies the calendar or aggregates into time buckets.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to answer 'when does liquidity arrive' instead of reading raw per-holding maturity dates.

novel_features.name: Obligor concentration
novel_features.description: Total credit exposure to each obligor as a share of the consolidated book, flagging self-set limit breaches.
novel_features.rationale: Rolls up holdings + open subscriptions by obligor across every entity and computes the share denominator; the API is strictly entity-scoped.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for group-wide counterparty risk; per-entity obligor-exposure calls cannot see the consolidated position.

novel_features.name: Consolidated group book
novel_features.description: One portfolio across every legal entity: total invested, weighted-average yield/maturity, currency split.
novel_features.rationale: Unions holdings across all mirrored entities with amount-weighted aggregates; API forces one-entity-per-call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for the group-treasurer view no single login or call returns.

narrative.headline: Every TreasurySpring read and write endpoint, plus a local SQLite mirror that answers portfolio-level questions no single API call can: maturity ladders, obligor concentration, and a consolidated group book.
narrative.value_prop: ts mirrors your entities, indications, holdings, subscriptions and obligor exposures into local SQLite, then joins across them offline. Run `ts ladder` for a settlement-adjusted cash-flow forecast, `ts concentration --by obligor` for group-wide credit risk, or `ts book` for the consolidated portfolio across every entity. Agent-native: --json, --select, typed exit codes.
narrative.auth_narrative: TreasurySpring uses OAuth2 client-credentials. Set TS_CLIENT_ID and TS_CLIENT_SECRET, then `ts auth login` exchanges them at /oauth/token for a bearer token cached locally. Alternatively set TS_BEARER_TOKEN with a pre-minted token. Use the sandbox with --base-url or TS_ENV=sandbox.

quickstart.comment: Health check: confirms config and reachability without needing a token.
Exchange client_id/secret for a bearer token.
Mirror entities, holdings, indications, subscriptions and events into local SQLite.
Settlement-adjusted cash-flow forecast across all entities.

troubleshoots.fix: Run `ts auth login` (or set TS_BEARER_TOKEN). Every endpoint, including health, needs a bearer token.
Run `ts sync` first; transcendence commands read the local mirror.

narrative.when_to_use: Use ts to inspect a TreasurySpring treasury book from the command line or an agent: list available products and yields, monitor live holdings, project cash flows by maturity, measure obligor concentration, and track lifecycle events. Best when you need portfolio-level answers that span entities or resources, or scriptable/offline access the portal and per-call API do not give.
anti_triggers: Do not use ts to place real subscriptions or change maturity actions unless the write surface was explicitly enabled and you intend to commit capital.
Do not use ts for non-TreasurySpring treasury data; it only mirrors the TreasurySpring Public API.
